takeaway: Neutrophils live only a few hours in inflamed tissue; a severe infection becomes a graveyard of neutrophils whose enzymes can damage host tissue.

question.text: With regard to neutrophils (polymorphonuclear leucocytes), which statement is true?
question.say: With regard to neutrophils, the polymorphonuclear leucocytes, which statement is true?

answer.text: They have a lifespan of only a few hours in inflamed tissue
answer.say: The answer is: they have a lifespan of only a few hours in inflamed tissue.

lines.text: Neutrophils: brave soldiers in the inflamed tissue.
lines.say: Meet the neutrophils, brave little soldiers rushing into the inflamed tissue.

lines.text: But their hourglass runs out fast.
lines.say: But look at the hourglass beside them. Their time runs out fast.

lines.text: Only a few hours in an inflammatory lesion, sometimes less.
lines.say: In an inflammatory lesion, a neutrophil lives only a few hours, and sometimes less.

lines.text: A severe infection becomes a graveyard of thousands of neutrophils.
lines.say: (sigh) So a severe local infection quickly becomes a graveyard of thousands of neutrophils.

lines.text: Their contents, especially enzymes, spill out and may damage host tissue.
lines.say: As they fall, their contents, especially their enzymes, spill out and may cause additional damage to host tissues.

lines.text: Remember: neutrophils live only a few hours in inflamed tissue.
lines.say: Remember: neutrophils have a lifespan of only a few hours in inflamed tissue.
